category.title: Warm-up
category.intro: A 10-minute moving warm-up you can do before any workout. First you raise your pulse, then you loosen your joints, and finally you prepare your muscles with light moves.
science: Before training, a moving (dynamic) warm-up is preferred over long static stretching; long static stretches can slightly reduce strength and jumping for a short while.
Dynamic stretching on its own has only a small effect on performance; the main benefit of a warm-up is raising body temperature and pulse.
Warm-ups shown to reduce injuries (e.g. FIFA 11+) have several parts: raising the pulse, loosening the joints and light strength moves. This warm-up follows the same order.
Evidence that stretching alone prevents injury is weak; a warm-up doesn't replace training, but it prepares you for it.

exercises.name: Marching on the Spot
steps: Lift one knee towards hip height and swing the opposite arm forward.
Lower your foot and lift the other knee.
Keep marching briskly and upright.
exercises.tip: Actively swinging your arms raises your pulse more.
exercises.mistake: Don't lean forward; keep your body upright.

exercises.name: Arm Circles
exercises.setup: Stand tall and open your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
steps: Draw small circles with your arms.
Slowly make the circles bigger.
Change direction halfway through.
exercises.tip: Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
exercises.mistake: Don't swing them fast and jerkily.

exercises.name: Step Jack
exercises.setup: Stand up, feet together, arms by your sides.
steps: Step out to the side with one foot while raising your arms above your head.
Return to the start.
Repeat stepping out to the other side.
exercises.tip: Jumping jacks without the jump; kind to your knees and your neighbours.
exercises.mistake: Don't hunch your shoulders towards your ears.

exercises.name: Torso Twist
exercises.setup: Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width. Bend your elbows and hold your hands at chest height.
steps: Keeping your hips facing forward, turn your torso and arms to the right.
Pass through the middle and turn to the left.
Keep going side to side with a smooth rhythm; make the turn a little bigger each time.
exercises.tip: Gently pivoting the heel of your back foot eases your knee.
exercises.mistake: Don't swing wildly; turn with control.

exercises.name: Leg Swings
exercises.target: Hips and back of the legs (mobility)
exercises.setup: Stand tall; support yourself with one hand on a wall or chair for balance.
steps: Swing your outside leg forward, straight and relaxed.
Let it swing back and behind you.
Keep going like a pendulum, making each swing a little bigger; switch legs halfway through.
exercises.tip: Keep your body upright and let the movement come from the hip.
exercises.mistake: Don't force your leg up as if kicking; keep the stretch gentle.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.setup: Get on all fours: hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips.
steps: As you breathe in, let your belly drop towards the floor and lift your chest and head.
As you breathe out, round your back towards the ceiling and bring your chin towards your chest.
Move slowly back and forth between the two.
exercises.tip: Ideal for warming up and cooling down.
exercises.mistake: Don't do it fast; one move per breath.

exercises.name: Inchworm
steps: Bend forward and put your hands on the floor in front of your feet; bend your knees if needed.
Walk your hands forward into a push-up position.
Walk your hands back towards your feet and stand up.
exercises.tip: It's also a great move for warming up.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your hips sag in the plank.

exercises.name: Squat
exercises.target: Front of the thighs, glutes and hamstrings
exercises.setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
steps: Push your hips back and lower down; reach your arms forward.
Stop when your thighs are close to parallel with the floor; chest up.
Push through your heels to stand up.
exercises.tip: Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your knees cave in or your heels lift off the floor.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.target: Front of the thighs and glutes
steps: Take a big step back with one foot and lower by bending both knees.
Stop when your back knee nears the floor; your front knee is over your ankle.
Push through your front heel to return to the start; switch legs halfway through.
exercises.tip: The reverse lunge is kinder to the knee than the forward lunge.
exercises.mistake: Don't lean your body forward; stay upright.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, soles of your feet on the floor hip-width apart. Arms by your sides.
steps: Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips off the floor; form a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Keep your glutes tight at the top.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Press through your heels; you can lift your toes slightly.

exercises.name: Butt Kicks
exercises.setup: Stand up with your arms bent at the elbows.
steps: Pull one heel towards your bottom.
As you lower that foot, pull the other heel up.
Keep going as if running or walking on the spot.
exercises.tip: If you're just starting out, do it without hopping, as if walking.

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.setup: Stand up with your arms bent at the elbows.
steps: Running on the spot, pull your knees up to hip height.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Swing your arms as if running; keep the rhythm.
exercises.tip: If it's too hard, switch to marching on the spot and speed up again once you've caught your breath.
exercises.mistake: Don't lean back; keep your body tilted slightly forward.
